references.text: God describes himself as the one who knows his people and leads them, just as Jesus says that he knows his sheep and they follow him.
The Lord promises to raise up a shepherd who will care for the people, a direct precursor to Jesus' self-understanding as the good shepherd whom the sheep listen to.
The psalm describes the Lord as a shepherd who leads the people, and that they follow him, which mirrors the dynamic in John 10:27 where the sheep hear his voice and follow the shepherd.
The prophet describes God's care as he gathers the lambs in his arms and leads those who have young ones, an image of the close relationship and leadership Jesus describes.
In the same chapter, Jesus describes how the shepherd calls his own sheep by name, and they hear his voice, which is the direct context for verse 27.
Jesus confirms again that he knows his sheep and they know him, a repetition of the mutual knowledge that is central to verse 27.
